w: London's TV mast stands on the hill where John Logie Baird ran a TV station and transmitter from 1933, three years before the Crystal Palace exhibition building burned down nearby. The hilltop, 109 metres up, is the highest ground in London; the tower is the city's eighth-tallest structure and its main TV transmitter.
s: London's tallest TV mast, on Baird's old test site
_facts: Site of John Logie Baird's TV station and transmitter from 1933
Stands on a 109-metre hill, the highest ground level in London
Eighth-tallest structure in London; the main TV transmitter for Greater London

w: At 56 hectares, this is Southwark's largest park -- and almost none of it started as parkland. Nearly all the ground was previously housing, industry and transport infrastructure before being cleared into open space, unusual for a London park this size, between Walworth, Bermondsey and Peckham.
s: Southwark's largest park, built over streets and factories
_facts: 56 hectares (140 acres); the largest park in the London Borough of Southwark
Carved out of previously built-up housing, industrial and transport land
Borders Walworth to the north, Bermondsey to the east and Peckham to the south

w: For 133 years Lambeth's archive lived at the Minet Library on Knatchbull Road; in February 2024 it moved to a purpose-built home at 16 Brixton Hill. Free to the public, it holds parish records, census returns, poll books, trade directories and old newspapers for tracing family history.
s: 133 years of Lambeth's paper trail, now on Brixton Hill
_facts: Housed at Minet Library for 133 years, until 2023
Reopened February 2024 in a new purpose-built building at 16 Brixton Hill
Holds parish records, census returns, poll books, trade directories, historic newspapers; free entry
